competency: Bring together the ideas of Unit 2.

keywords.def: Anything that has mass and occupies space.
The mixing and spreading out of a substance because its particles move.
A single kind of matter that cannot be separated by physical means.
A physical combination of two or more pure substances.
A change in appearance, not composition.

en.text: Matter has mass and occupies space. It is made of tiny moving particles and exists as solid, liquid or gas. States change by adding or removing energy. Matter is pure (elements and compounds) or a mixture (homogeneous or heterogeneous). Changes are physical or chemical. Mixtures are separated by physical methods.

root.label: Matter
root.info: Anything that has mass and occupies space.

children.label: Pure substance
children.info: A single kind of matter. It cannot be separated by physical means.

children.label: Element
children.info: One kind of atom. Cannot be broken down by ordinary chemical means. Metals (iron, gold) and non-metals (oxygen, sulfur).

children.label: Compound
children.info: Elements chemically combined in a definite proportion by mass. Examples: water, table salt.

children.label: Mixture
children.info: Two or more pure substances physically combined. Separated by physical methods.

children.label: Homogeneous
children.info: Uniform composition, one phase: a solution. Examples: air, salt solution, brass.

children.label: Heterogeneous
children.info: Not uniform; parts can be seen. Examples: soil, milk, oil and water.

screens.title: Key words of the unit
defs: Anything that has mass and occupies space.
A single kind of matter that cannot be separated by physical means.
A physical combination of two or more pure substances.
A change in appearance, not composition.

screens.why:
Melting: solid → liquid. Freezing is the reverse: liquid → solid.
Evaporation: liquid → gas. Condensation is the reverse: gas → liquid.
Sublimation: solid → gas directly. Deposition is the reverse: gas → solid.
screens.text: Review Part III: match each change of state to what happens.
What is matter? All of the following are matter EXCEPT …
screens.why:
Matter has mass and occupies space.
A plant, a stone and air all have mass and take up space.
Sound has no mass: it is a form of energy.
So sound is not matter.

screens.text: True or false? Elements can be further decomposed by ordinary chemical means.
screens.why:
An element has only one kind of atom.
By definition, it cannot be broken down by ordinary chemical means.
Compounds can be broken down; elements cannot. So false.

screens.text: Spot the false statement: which statement is FALSE?
opts: A compound has a fixed composition
A homogeneous mixture has one phase
screens.why:
A compound has a fixed composition: true.
A homogeneous mixture has one phase: true.
Physical changes are easily reversed: true.
Diffusion is fastest in gases and very, very slow in solids. So "fastest in solids" is false.

items.text: True or false? Depending upon the temperature, water can exist in solid, liquid or gas states.
items.why:
Below 0 °C water is ice: solid.
Between 0 °C and 100 °C it is liquid water.
At 100 °C it boils to steam: gas.
So the statement is true.

items.text: True or false? A gas has neither a definite volume nor a definite shape.
items.why:
Gas particles are far apart and move freely.
A gas spreads out to fill any container.
So it takes the shape and the volume of its container. True.

items.text: True or false? A heterogeneous mixture contains one phase.
items.why:
A heterogeneous mixture has visible parts with boundaries.
Each part is a phase, so it has two or more phases.
Example: oil and water form two layers. So false.

items.text: Particles and states: which of the following decreases during the changes solid → liquid → gas?
items.why:
From solid to liquid to gas, particles gain energy.
They move faster and spread further apart.
So energy, speed and distance all increase.
Only the degree of order decreases: gas particles are the least orderly.

items.text: Properties of solids: which of the following is not a property of solids?
items.why:
Solids have a definite shape and volume.
They are very hard to compress and diffuse very little.
A fluid is something that flows. Only liquids and gases flow.
So "solids are fluids" is not true.

items.text: What decides the state? The physical state of a substance depends on …
items.why:
Temperature: heating ice makes it melt.
Pressure: squeezing a gas can turn it into a liquid.
Intermolecular force: strong forces hold particles together as a solid.
All three matter, so the answer is "all".

items.text: Which of the following has no definite shape and volume?
items.why:
Only a gas has no definite shape and no definite volume.
Water is a liquid: definite volume.
Iron and gold are solids: definite shape and volume.
Carbon dioxide is a gas, so it is the answer.

items.text: Which two states of matter are fluids?
items.why:
A fluid is matter that can flow.
Liquids flow and take the shape of their container.
Gases flow and spread out.
Solids do not flow. So liquid and gas are fluids.

items.ask: Changes of state in nature: when rain falls, it is because water vapour in the clouds is condensing into liquid ___.
items.why:
Water vapour is a gas.
High in the sky it cools and condenses: gas → liquid.
The tiny drops join and fall as rain.
So the vapour becomes liquid water.

items.ask: Name the separation technique: heating a solution until the liquid becomes a gas, leaving a solid, is ___.
items.why:
The liquid is heated and escapes as vapour.
The dissolved solid is left behind.
This is evaporation, as in getting salt from salt water.
items.clue: Think of getting salt from salt water.
